content.text:
I submitted index 2 (Ni0.83Sb0.17) as the best composition. Its EQE was 0.042%, about 30 times higher than either of the other two I measured. All 3 merit measurements are used, so I can't tell whether a composition near index 2 would do better. Indices 1 and 3 are the obvious ones to test if more budget is available.

| Index | Ni : Sb | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 19 | 0.34 : 0.66 (the NiSb2O6 composition) | 0.0013 |
| 2 | 0.83 : 0.17 | **0.042** |
| 0 | 0.86 : 0.14 (most Ni-rich) | 0.0014 |

- **Index 19 first:** NiSb2O6 is the stable mixed Ni–Sb oxide (the MACE model puts it at zero energy above the stability limit), and the XRD pattern at index 19 matched it best. Its EQE was very low anyway.
- **Index 2 second:** I moved to the Ni-rich side, which gave the best result.
- **Index 0 last:** I expected the rise toward Ni to continue, but EQE fell back to about the index 19 level. The good region looks narrow, around 17% Sb, but three points are too few to confirm that.

The model predictions didn't help much in this case:
- **Band gaps:** MEGNet gave NiSb2O6 a gap of 0.04 eV, which isn't physical for this compound, so I ignored it. It gave NiSb2O4 3.6 eV.
- **NiO stability:** MACE put NiO 0.41 eV/atom above the stability limit, which looks like an artifact.
- **Measurement choices:** after the first measurement, I picked compositions from the measured trend, not from the models.
- **XRD:** the patterns at indices 6, 19 and 26 all looked like the same rutile-type structure. They didn't separate the compositions, and I used only 3 of the 5 XRD measurements.
